changes.before: Define Panel to show its Notice h2 and its children. App should put a paragraph reading Bring a bottle. inside Panel.
changes.after: Use children to place supplied content inside a shared wrapper.

before: A wrapper can provide a surrounding structure while its caller supplies the content inside. JSX nested between a component’s opening and closing tags becomes its children prop. The wrapper need not know every kind of content it will receive.

Define Panel to show its Notice h2 and its children. App should put a paragraph reading Bring a bottle. inside Panel. The starter is the small application to edit; the examples above remain available for comparison.
after: A wrapper is a component that surrounds other content. JSX placed between its opening and closing tags arrives in a prop named `children`.
The same `Panel` can receive a button or another element instead of a paragraph. It keeps its heading and shows the new content where `{props.children}` appears.
Make `Panel` show an `<h2>` that says `Notice`, followed by its children. In `App`, put a paragraph saying `Bring a bottle.` inside `Panel`.

before: Read the small example and explain its inputs and effects.
Complete the starter for this lesson.
Run the behavior checks, then predict a changed case.
after: Keep the Notice heading inside Panel.
Put the requested paragraph inside Panel and run the checks.

before: Trace the visible input, event and resulting screen before changing the code.
after: The content between `<Panel>` and `</Panel>` becomes children.

before.question: If App uses Closed today, must Panel be rewritten to support strong?
choices: No; props.children carries the supplied strong element
No; the strong element is discarded automatically
before.explanation: The wrapper inserts the received React content; it does not restrict that content to the earlier paragraph.

after.question: Does Panel need new code to show `Closed today` as its child?
choices: No. props.children carries the supplied strong element.
No. React removes the strong element.
after.explanation: Panel places the content it receives below its heading.

project.title: Children compose a wrapper
project.task: Make Panel show a Notice h2 and its children. Put a paragraph saying Bring a bottle. inside it.
project.done_when: The notice heading and supplied paragraph appear together inside the panel.
